definitions.explanation: The act of creating false information, data, or evidence and presenting it as true; falsification.

examples.japanese: データを{捏造|ねつぞう}する。
この{記事|きじ}は{捏造|ねつぞう}だと{判明|はんめい}した。
examples.english: This article turned out to be fabricated.

examples.japanese: {研究|けんきゅう}{不正|ふせい}で{論文|ろんぶん}の{捏造|ねつぞう}が{発覚|はっかく}した。
examples.english: Fabrication of the research paper was discovered as academic misconduct.

notes:
COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
・データを{捏造|ねつぞう}する - to fabricate data
・{証拠|しょうこ}を{捏造|ねつぞう}する - to forge evidence
・{歴史|れきし}の{捏造|ねつぞう} - falsification of history
・{論文|ろんぶん}{捏造|ねつぞう} - research fraud/fabrication

USAGE CONTEXT:
Common in news reporting about scandals, academic misconduct, or legal cases.

RELATED WORDS:
・{改竄|かいざん} - falsification, tampering (altering existing documents)
・{歪曲|わいきょく} - distortion, misrepresentation
・{偽造|ぎぞう} - forgery, counterfeiting (especially documents, money)
